LM Studio has added Z.ai's new GLM-5.3-Flash model to its AI agent platform Bionic, bringing multimodal input, a 1 million token context window, and pricing far lower than GLM-5.2. Here are the details.

LM Studio quickly adds GLM-5.3-Flash to Bionic

Since its initial announcement in mid-July, LM Studio has continued to expand the models and features on the Bionic platform. Designed for Mac and Windows, this platform is primarily used for agentic tasks such as coding, research, and document handling.

LM Studio Bionic can use locally run models, or it can choose cloud-based models hosted on servers within the United States, with the latter strictly adhering to a zero data retention policy.

Shortly after LM Studio Bionic went live, the company added support for Moonshot AI's Kimi K3. Today, the company officially launched cloud support for Z.ai's new GLM-5.3-Flash model, which LM Studio says costs up to 10 times less to run than GLM-5.2.

LM Studio's announcement came just hours before the official release of GLM-5.3-Flash, and the model had previously been tested anonymously under the code name "Ox Alpha" on OpenCode and OpenRouter, attracting considerable attention.

GLM-5.3-Flash is a 320 billion parameter mixture-of-experts model with 18 billion active parameters per run, supporting image and text input, with a 1 million token context window.

In the benchmarks highlighted by Z.ai, GLM-5.3-Flash outperforms GLM-5.2, and its overall performance is roughly on par with frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and DeepSeek.

To learn how to use GLM-5.3-Flash on LM Studio Bionic, you can follow this link for more information.
